tracks.legalName: Motion to Expunge Record of Arrest That Did Not Result in a Conviction (La. C.Cr.P. art. 976)
tracks.publicName: Clear an arrest that did not end in a conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: Article 976(A) lets a person move to expunge a record of arrest for a felony or misdemeanour that did not result in conviction where the person was not prosecuted and the time limitation has expired, the district attorney declined to prosecute every offence arising out of the arrest including because a pretrial diversion programme was completed, the proceedings were finally disposed of by dismissal, sustaining of a motion to quash or acquittal, or the person was judicially determined to be factually innocent and entitled to compensation under R.S. 15:572.8. Article 976(B) bars expungement of an arrest for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, or a parish or municipal equivalent, where the person was placed in a pretrial diversion programme, until five years have elapsed since the date of arrest. Article 975 bars filing by a person in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour. Relief is effectively mandatory: under Article 980 the court grants where no timely objection is filed and the mover is legally entitled.

exclusions: A person in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour may not file the motion (Art. 975). This is a status bar that lifts when custody status changes, not a permanent eligibility bar.

An arrest for operating a vehicle while intoxicated under R.S. 14:98, or a parish or municipal ordinance equivalent, where the person was placed in a pretrial diversion programme, until five years have elapsed from the date of arrest (Art. 976(B)).
A conviction arising out of the arrest. Any charge on the arrest that resulted in a misdemeanour or felony conviction is outside this Article and belongs to Article 977 or Article 978.

waitingPeriods.condition: Arrest for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, or a parish or municipal ordinance equivalent, where the person entered a pretrial diversion programme
waitingPeriods.duration: Five years from the date of arrest for that offence (Art. 976(B)). The Article 989 form carries a dedicated check-box for it.
None. There is no waiting period; where prosecution was never instituted the ground is the expiry of the time limitation for prosecution itself.

geography.venue: The court with trial jurisdiction over the offence in the parish of arrest, under Article 972.1: district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts.

destination.name: Clerk of court for the parish of arrest
destination.detail: File the Article 989 motion with the proposed Article 991 and Article 992 orders. The clerk collects the Article 983 fees at filing unless a returned Article 988 fee exemption is appended, and thereafter serves the district attorney, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting agency under Article 979.

components.notes: The Article 989 Motion for Expungement. Part I is defendant information; Part II is arrest information, and the section for arrests that did not result in conviction carries eligibility check-boxes that track Article 976(A) directly, plus the Article 976(B) vehicle-while-intoxicated diversion box. The Part II eligibility selection is a legal conclusion the participant owns — Louisiana State Police names choosing the wrong eligibility basis as a common fatal error. Mandatory under Article 986.

The Article 991 Order. It sets the sixty-day objection window for the district attorney and the arresting agency and for the Bureau, directs the clerk to serve, and states that no contradictory hearing is required where an Affidavit of No Opposition executed by each named agency is attached. Every judicial field is left blank.
The Article 992 Order of Expungement of Arrest/Conviction Record — the final order. Every decretal and judicial field is left blank.

components.notes: Article 993 is the statutory supplemental sheet, and Article 986(B) permits supplemental forms so long as they adhere to it. It is a participant-completed continuation sheet with the same eligibility check-boxes as the motion, grouped by arrests that did not result in conviction, misdemeanour convictions and felony convictions. Retained by Edition 1.1 as a source-gated asset. Its absence would restrict only multi-count cases; a single-count packet does not need it. Output strategy corrected to custom_pleading by rcap-la-arts-993-995-998-output-strategy-memo-correction, against the adjudication at rcap-la-arts-993-995-998-html-source-output-strategy-adjudication. There is no official PDF of this article: the Legislature publishes the controlling text as HTML on its own article page, and the retained capture is a browser print of that page rather than an issuer publication, so official_pdf_fill can only resolve to a missing source. process_guidance is equally wrong, because a participant submission exists on this component. The article remains the authority and the source identity, which is why officialFormId and officialSourceUrl are kept. Article 986(A) makes the statutory forms exclusive, so the rendering must reproduce the Legislature's own words rather than paraphrase them, and under Article 986(C) the court name is the only authorized variation. The Louisiana Supreme Court's local city and parish packet is not a statewide substitute and must not be used as one. No template exists yet, none is counsel-approved, and no implementation is authorized here. Article 993 is one statutory sheet carrying three Yes/No sections — arrests without conviction, misdemeanour convictions and felony convictions — so a template must render it as a single sheet and must not be split into three. The Article 986(B) adherence requirement is unchanged: a supplemental form is permitted only so far as it adheres to the statutory form. The sheet is participant-completed throughout.

Sequencing is the deliverable in Louisiana. The instructions carry, in order: order the Right to Review or sheriff's background check and watch its sixty-day life; complete the participant fields of the Article 988 fee exemption and deliver it to the district attorney BEFORE filing, expecting it back within fifteen days; request whichever Article 989 certification letters the chosen eligibility basis needs; file with the clerk with the fee or the returned exemption; the clerk serves the district attorney, the Bureau and the arresting agency under Article 979; agencies have sixty days from service to object under Article 980, extendable once by up to thirty days; an Affidavit of No Opposition from each named agency attached to the motion supports an ex parte grant with no contradictory hearing; if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment under Article 982. It also carries the Louisiana State Police list of common fatal errors: wrong arrest date, using the amended charge instead of the original arrest charge, omitting counts, putting misdemeanours and felonies in the wrong section, missing dispositions or certifications, and choosing the wrong eligibility basis.

rules.filing: File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.
rules.notice: Under Article 980 any entity served under Article 979 may object by filing an affidavit of response, with reasons and with service on the defendant, within sixty days from the date of service of the motion. Since 1 August 2015 the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information is on the same sixty-day period as everyone else. Article 980(C) lets the court grant one extension of not more than thirty days beyond the original sixty. A timely objection means a contradictory hearing, which the objecting party must ask to have set. Where an Affidavit of No Opposition executed by each named agency is attached to the motion, the Article 991 Order states that no contradictory hearing is required and the motion may be granted ex parte.
rules.service: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.
rules.participantSignature: The mover signs the Article 989 Motion in the block headed 'If not represented by counsel'. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.
rules.fees: Article 983(A) caps the total cost of obtaining a court order of expungement at five hundred fifty dollars. The clerk collects at the time of filing and Article 983 makes the fees non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Article 983(F) waives all fees where a district attorney certification verifies no felony convictions and no pending felony charge under a bill of information or indictment, together with one of the listed non-conviction grounds — acquittal of all charges after trial including lesser and included offences, no prosecution within the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, dismissal or refusal before the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, factual innocence with entitlement to compensation under R.S. 15:572.8, or a juvenile who completed a juvenile drug court programme and is exempt under Article 983(G). The exemption is very often available on this track and must be screened before filing rather than after.
rules.feeWaiver: Article 983(F), claimed through the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption. The form goes to the district attorney before filing and comes back within fifteen days. Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony.

selfHelpStopConditions: Any named agency files an Article 990 affidavit of response objecting to the motion.
The court sets a contradictory hearing under Article 980(D).
The record of the arrest names anyone besides the participant, which is the Article 985 redaction question and routes to the redaction track rather than this one.
The participant is in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour, so Article 975 bars filing.
The disposition of any charge on the arrest is unclear, or the rap sheet and the court record disagree.
The arrest spans more than one parish, so more than one court has trial jurisdiction.
Any charge on the arrest ended in a conviction.
The arrest was vehicle-while-intoxicated in any form.
A charge is pending against the participant.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Expunge a Record of Arrest and Conviction of a Misdemeanor Offense (La. C.Cr.P. art. 977)

controllingAuthority.summary: Article 977(A) lets a person move to expunge a record of arrest and conviction of a misdemeanour on either of two grounds. Under (A)(1) the conviction was set aside and the prosecution dismissed under Article 894(B), which is the separate Article 987 mechanism. Under (A)(2) more than five years have elapsed since the person completed any sentence, deferred adjudication, or period of probation or parole, the person has not been convicted of any felony offence during that five-year period and has no felony charge pending; the motion must include a certification obtained from the district attorney verifying, to his knowledge, no felony convictions during the five-year period and no pending felony charges under a bill of information or indictment. Article 977(C) bars expungement where the misdemeanour conviction arose from circumstances involving or resulting from an arrest for a sex offence as defined in R.S. 15:541 — expressly preserving interim expungement under Article 985.1 — and where the conviction was for domestic abuse battery or for stalking under R.S. 14:40.2. Confirmed against the current official text, whose source notes run through Acts 2023, No. 342.

exclusions: A misdemeanour conviction that arose from circumstances involving, or is the result of, an arrest for a sex offence as defined in R.S. 15:541. Article 977(C)(1) expressly preserves interim expungement under Article 985.1, so the felony-arrest entry may still be cleared on the interim track even though the misdemeanour itself may not.
A misdemeanour conviction for domestic abuse battery (Art. 977(C)(2)).
A misdemeanour conviction for stalking under R.S. 14:40.2 (Art. 977(C)(3)).
A person in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour may not file (Art. 975).
A first-offence possession of marijuana, tetrahydrocannabinol or chemical derivatives misdemeanour conviction is governed by Article 977(D) and its own Article 998 form, and is a separate track.

Sequencing is the deliverable in Louisiana. The instructions carry, in order: order the Right to Review or sheriff's background check and watch its sixty-day life; complete the participant fields of the Article 988 fee exemption and deliver it to the district attorney BEFORE filing, expecting it back within fifteen days; request whichever Article 989 certification letters the chosen eligibility basis needs; file with the clerk with the fee or the returned exemption; the clerk serves the district attorney, the Bureau and the arresting agency under Article 979; agencies have sixty days from service to object under Article 980, extendable once by up to thirty days; an Affidavit of No Opposition from each named agency attached to the motion supports an ex parte grant with no contradictory hearing; if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment under Article 982. rules.filing: File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.
rules.notice: Under Article 980 any entity served under Article 979 may object by filing an affidavit of response, with reasons and with service on the defendant, within sixty days from the date of service of the motion. Since 1 August 2015 the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information is on the same sixty-day period as everyone else. Article 980(C) lets the court grant one extension of not more than thirty days beyond the original sixty. A timely objection means a contradictory hearing, which the objecting party must ask to have set. Where an Affidavit of No Opposition executed by each named agency is attached to the motion, the Article 991 Order states that no contradictory hearing is required and the motion may be granted ex parte.
rules.service: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.
rules.participantSignature: The mover signs the Article 989 Motion in the block headed 'If not represented by counsel'. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.
rules.fees: Article 983(A) caps the total cost at five hundred fifty dollars, collected by the clerk at filing and non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Where the conviction is for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, Article 984(C) assesses a further fifty-dollar court cost payable to the Office of Motor Vehicles.
rules.feeWaiver: Article 983(F) through the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, but its grounds are non-conviction grounds, so it is rarely available on a conviction track. Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony.

rules.notice: Under Article 980 any entity served under Article 979 may object by filing an affidavit of response, with reasons and with service on the defendant, within sixty days from the date of service of the motion. Since 1 August 2015 the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information is on the same sixty-day period as everyone else. Article 980(C) lets the court grant one extension of not more than thirty days beyond the original sixty. tracks.legalName: Motion to Expunge Record of Arrest and Conviction of a Felony Offense (La. C.Cr.P. art. 978)

controllingAuthority.summary: Article 978(A) lets a person move to expunge a record of arrest and conviction of a felony where the conviction was set aside and the prosecution dismissed under Article 893(E); or where more than ten years have elapsed since the person completed any sentence, deferred adjudication, or period of probation or parole, the person has not been convicted of any other criminal offence during that ten-year period and has no criminal charge pending, with a district attorney certification; or where the person is entitled to a first offender pardon for the offence, provided it is not a crime of violence or a sex offence. Article 978(B) bars expungement, and bars filing, where the person was convicted of the commission or attempted commission of a crime of violence under R.S. 14:2(B) unless Paragraph E applies; a sex offence or a criminal offence against a victim who is a minor under R.S. 15:541, with a narrow carnal-knowledge exception; a violation of the Uniform Controlled Dangerous Substances Law, except five listed categories that may be expunged; or domestic abuse battery. Article 978(E) permits the court, after a contradictory hearing, to order expungement for aggravated battery, second degree battery, aggravated criminal damage to property, simple robbery, purse snatching, or illegal use of weapons or dangerous instrumentalities on the ten-year clean-period conditions. Read against the current official text, whose source notes now run through Acts 2024, No. 580.

exclusions: A crime of violence as defined by or enumerated in R.S. 14:2(B), unless the offence is one of the six named in Article 978(E) and the court grants relief after a contradictory hearing (Art. 978(B)(1)).

Notwithstanding any provision of Article 893, a sex offence or a criminal offence against a victim who is a minor as each is defined by R.S. 15:541, or any offence occurring before 18 June 1992 that would be so defined had it occurred on or after that date (Art. 978(B)(2)(a)).

A violation of the Uniform Controlled Dangerous Substances Law (Art. 978(B)(3)), except any of the following, which may be expunged: possession of a controlled dangerous substance under R.S. 40:966(C), 967(C), 968(C), 969(C) or 970(C); possession with intent to distribute; a violation punishable by a term of imprisonment of not more than five years; a violation that may be expunged under Article 893(E); and a violation for which the person is entitled to a first offender pardon under La. Const. art. IV, § 5(E)(1).
A conviction for domestic abuse battery (Art. 978(B)(4)).
A first offender pardon route is unavailable where the offence is a crime of violence or a sex offence (Art. 978(A)(3)).
A person in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour may not file (Art. 975).

More than ten years from completion of any sentence, deferred adjudication, or period of probation or parole, with no conviction of ANY OTHER CRIMINAL OFFENCE during that ten-year period and no criminal charge pending. This is not the misdemeanour test with a larger number: the misdemeanour clean period bars felony convictions only, and this one bars any criminal offence.

Under R.S. 15:572 a first offender never previously convicted of a felony is automatically pardoned on completion of sentence without a Board of Pardons recommendation or gubernatorial action, but no pardon issues unless the court costs for the conviction are paid.

components.notes: Article 993 is the statutory supplemental sheet, and Article 986(B) permits supplemental forms so long as they adhere to it. It is a participant-completed continuation sheet with the same eligibility check-boxes as the motion, grouped by arrests that did not result in conviction, misdemeanour convictions and felony convictions. Retained by Edition 1.1 as a source-gated asset. Its absence would restrict only multi-count cases; a single-count packet does not need it. Output strategy corrected to custom_pleading by rcap-la-arts-993-995-998-output-strategy-memo-correction, against the adjudication at rcap-la-arts-993-995-998-html-source-output-strategy-adjudication. There is no official PDF of this article: the Legislature publishes the controlling text as HTML on its own article page, and the retained capture is a browser print of that page rather than an issuer publication, so official_pdf_fill can only resolve to a missing source. process_guidance is equally wrong, because a participant submission exists on this component. The article remains the authority and the source identity, which is why officialFormId and officialSourceUrl are kept. Article 986(A) makes the statutory forms exclusive, so the rendering must reproduce the Legislature's own words rather than paraphrase them, and under Article 986(C) the court name is the only authorized variation. The Louisiana Supreme Court's local city and parish packet is not a statewide substitute and must not be used as one. No template exists yet, none is counsel-approved, and no implementation is authorized here. Article 993 is one statutory sheet carrying three Yes/No sections — arrests without conviction, misdemeanour convictions and felony convictions — so a template must render it as a single sheet and must not be split into three. The Article 986(B) adherence requirement is unchanged: a supplemental form is permitted only so far as it adheres to the statutory form. The sheet is participant-completed throughout.

Conditional to vehicle-while-intoxicated cases only, and never a gate on an unrelated Louisiana track.

Sequencing is the deliverable in Louisiana. The instructions carry, in order: order the Right to Review or sheriff's background check and watch its sixty-day life; complete the participant fields of the Article 988 fee exemption and deliver it to the district attorney BEFORE filing, expecting it back within fifteen days; request whichever Article 989 certification letters the chosen eligibility basis needs; file with the clerk with the fee or the returned exemption; the clerk serves the district attorney, the Bureau and the arresting agency under Article 979; agencies have sixty days from service to object under Article 980, extendable once by up to thirty days; an Affidavit of No Opposition from each named agency attached to the motion supports an ex parte grant with no contradictory hearing; if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment under Article 982. It also carries the Louisiana State Police list of common fatal errors: wrong arrest date, using the amended charge instead of the original arrest charge, omitting counts, putting misdemeanours and felonies in the wrong section, missing dispositions or certifications, and choosing the wrong eligibility basis. On this track the instructions carry a prominent attorney-review notice on every felony without exception; the Article 987 routing rule where Article 893(E) relief has not occurred, with the Article 987 packet referenced rather than duplicated; the first-offender-pardon court-costs question and how to fix unpaid costs; and a plain statement that an Article 978(E) contradictory hearing, an agency objection, or any contested factual question is where self-help ends and a lawyer takes over.

rules.filing: File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.
rules.notice: Under Article 980 any entity served under Article 979 may object by filing an affidavit of response, with reasons and with service on the defendant, within sixty days from the date of service of the motion. Since 1 August 2015 the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information is on the same sixty-day period as everyone else. Article 980(C) lets the court grant one extension of not more than thirty days beyond the original sixty. A timely objection means a contradictory hearing, which the objecting party must ask to have set. Where an Affidavit of No Opposition executed by each named agency is attached to the motion, the Article 991 Order states that no contradictory hearing is required and the motion may be granted ex parte. On the Article 978(E) lane a contradictory hearing is required by the Article itself, so the ex parte route is not available there and the objection window is not the operative constraint.
rules.service: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.
rules.participantSignature: The mover signs the Article 989 Motion in the block headed 'If not represented by counsel'. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.
rules.fees: Article 983(A) caps the total cost at five hundred fifty dollars, collected by the clerk at filing and non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Where the conviction is for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, Article 984(C) assesses a further fifty-dollar court cost payable to the Office of Motor Vehicles. On the first offender pardon route the participant must also have paid the underlying court costs of the conviction, which is a precondition of the pardon rather than an expungement fee.
rules.feeWaiver: Article 983(F) through the Article 988 form in principle, but Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony. On a felony conviction track the exemption will almost never be available, and the packet says so rather than implying a waiver that will be refused.

selfHelpStopConditions: Every felony conviction. Counsel requires attorney review before filing on this track without exception, and the packet carries that instruction prominently.
The Article 978(E) violent-offence lane, which requires a contradictory hearing and a discretionary judicial finding. Hand off before filing.

Any offence that might be a crime of violence under R.S. 14:2(B) or a sex offence or offence against a minor victim under R.S. 15:541.

tracks.legalName: Interim Motion to Expunge a Felony Arrest from Criminal History (La. C.Cr.P. art. 985.1)
tracks.publicName: Clear a felony arrest that ended in a misdemeanor conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: Article 985.1(A) permits an interim motion to expunge a felony arrest from the criminal history of a person who was convicted of a misdemeanour offence arising out of that original felony arrest; only the original felony arrest is expunged. Article 985.1(B) makes the interim motion separate and distinct from expungement of a final conviction under Articles 976, 977 and 978. Article 985.1(C) applies the Article 979 et seq. procedures and fees except as provided in (D), and Article 985.1(D) provides that the motion is not subject to the time limitations of Article 977(A)(2) or 978(A)(2) and permits more than one interim expungement. Article 977(C)(1) expressly preserves interim expungement even where the misdemeanour conviction itself is barred by the sex-offence exclusion. Article 986 makes Article 994 the motion form and Article 995 the order form. Confirmed against the current official text; Article 985.1 has not been amended since Acts 2014, No. 145.

exclusions: The misdemeanour conviction itself is not expunged by this track. Only the original felony arrest entry is removed from the criminal history; the misdemeanour conviction remains on the record unless it is separately cleared under Article 977.
A person in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour may not file (Art. 975).
There is no case-count limitation. Article 985.1(D) expressly permits more than one interim expungement.

components.notes: The Article 994 Motion for Interim Expungement. Parallel in structure to Article 989, it cites Article 985.1 and asks the mover to identify the felony arrest that resulted in a misdemeanour conviction. It requires a criminal background check from Louisiana State Police or the parish sheriff dated within the past sixty days. Mandatory under Article 986.

The Article 995 Order of Expungement of Interim Arrest Record — the proposed final order the mover files with the motion, exactly as Articles 991 and 992 accompany the Article 989 motion. It orders the Bureau to expunge the entry of the named felony charges from the criminal history and orders the clerk, district attorney and arresting agency to expunge them from public indices. LegalEase supplies the caption and the felony charge identifiers only; the grant-or-deny selection, the two denial-reason boxes — that the mover was not arrested for a felony, and that the mover was not convicted of a misdemeanour offence — and the date, place and judge's signature are all left blank. Retained by Edition 1.1 as a source-gated asset. Output strategy corrected to custom_pleading by rcap-la-arts-993-995-998-output-strategy-memo-correction, against the adjudication at rcap-la-arts-993-995-998-html-source-output-strategy-adjudication. There is no official PDF of this article: the Legislature publishes the controlling text as HTML on its own article page, and the retained capture is a browser print of that page rather than an issuer publication, so official_pdf_fill can only resolve to a missing source. process_guidance is equally wrong, because a participant submission exists on this component. The article remains the authority and the source identity, which is why officialFormId and officialSourceUrl are kept. Article 986(A) makes the statutory forms exclusive, so the rendering must reproduce the Legislature's own words rather than paraphrase them, and under Article 986(C) the court name is the only authorized variation. The Louisiana Supreme Court's local city and parish packet is not a statewide substitute and must not be used as one. No template exists yet, none is counsel-approved, and no implementation is authorized here. The judicial boundary is unchanged by the strategy and is the controlling constraint on any template: the judge signs, so the rendering carries no signature label at all, and every decretal election, the granted-or-denied choice, both reasons-for-denial boxes, the date, the place and the judge's signature must render blank. LegalEase supplies the caption and the felony charge identifiers and nothing else.

Sequencing is the deliverable in Louisiana. The instructions carry, in order: order the Right to Review or sheriff's background check and watch its sixty-day life; complete the participant fields of the Article 988 fee exemption and deliver it to the district attorney BEFORE filing, expecting it back within fifteen days; request whichever Article 989 certification letters the chosen eligibility basis needs; file with the clerk with the fee or the returned exemption; the clerk serves the district attorney, the Bureau and the arresting agency under Article 979; agencies have sixty days from service to object under Article 980, extendable once by up to thirty days; an Affidavit of No Opposition from each named agency attached to the motion supports an ex parte grant with no contradictory hearing; if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment under Article 982. It also carries the Louisiana State Police list of common fatal errors: wrong arrest date, using the amended charge instead of the original arrest charge, omitting counts, putting misdemeanours and felonies in the wrong section, missing dispositions or certifications, and choosing the wrong eligibility basis. On this track the instructions make two things explicit: this motion clears only the original felony arrest entry, and the misdemeanour conviction stays on the record unless it is separately cleared under Article 977; and the route remains open where Article 977 is closed by the sex-offence exclusion, has no waiting period, and has no numerical cap.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: The review approved Track E with limitations and the current official text confirms it throughout. The route expunges only the original felony arrest from the criminal history and leaves the misdemeanour conviction in place unless it is separately cleared. tracks.legalName: Expungement by Redaction of Records with References to Multiple Individuals (La. C.Cr.P. art. 985)
tracks.publicName: Remove your name from a record you share with someone else

controllingAuthority.summary: Article 985(A) provides that if a record includes the name of more than one individual and one or more of them is entitled to an expungement of an arrest or conviction under Title XXXIV, any individual so entitled may petition the court to have records related to that individual's arrest or conviction expunged by redaction. Article 985(B) provides that if the court grants expungement by redaction, the name of the individual and all other identifying information regarding that individual shall be redacted from all records regarding the arrest and conviction, and the redacted records remain available for public access. Article 985(C) relieves the clerk of liability where the order does not specifically identify all locations of the records to be expunged or specify the information to be redacted. Article 972(3) defines the term. The relief runs on the Article 989 motion and the Article 992 order, whose text contains the dedicated redaction paragraph. Confirmed against the current official text; Article 985 has not been amended since Acts 2014, No. 145.

exclusions: A person who is not independently entitled to an expungement of the arrest or conviction under Title XXXIV. Article 985 is a form of relief for someone already entitled under Article 976, 977 or 978; it is not an independent eligibility ground.
A record that names only the petitioner. Where no other individual appears in the record there is nothing to redact and the ordinary expungement track applies instead.
A person in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour may not file (Art. 975).

Its text carries a dedicated paragraph granting expungement by redaction under Article 985 where the record includes more than one individual, which is what makes this track operable through the ordinary form set. components.notes: Article 993 is the statutory supplemental sheet, and Article 986(B) permits supplemental forms so long as they adhere to it. It is a participant-completed continuation sheet with the same eligibility check-boxes as the motion, grouped by arrests that did not result in conviction, misdemeanour convictions and felony convictions. Retained by Edition 1.1 as a source-gated asset. Its absence would restrict only multi-count cases; a single-count packet does not need it. Output strategy corrected to custom_pleading by rcap-la-arts-993-995-998-output-strategy-memo-correction, against the adjudication at rcap-la-arts-993-995-998-html-source-output-strategy-adjudication. There is no official PDF of this article: the Legislature publishes the controlling text as HTML on its own article page, and the retained capture is a browser print of that page rather than an issuer publication, so official_pdf_fill can only resolve to a missing source. process_guidance is equally wrong, because a participant submission exists on this component. The article remains the authority and the source identity, which is why officialFormId and officialSourceUrl are kept. Article 986(A) makes the statutory forms exclusive, so the rendering must reproduce the Legislature's own words rather than paraphrase them, and under Article 986(C) the court name is the only authorized variation. The Louisiana Supreme Court's local city and parish packet is not a statewide substitute and must not be used as one. No template exists yet, none is counsel-approved, and no implementation is authorized here. Article 993 is one statutory sheet carrying three Yes/No sections — arrests without conviction, misdemeanour convictions and felony convictions — so a template must render it as a single sheet and must not be split into three. The Article 986(B) adherence requirement is unchanged: a supplemental form is permitted only so far as it adheres to the statutory form. The sheet is participant-completed throughout.

Sequencing is the deliverable in Louisiana. The instructions carry, in order: order the Right to Review or sheriff's background check and watch its sixty-day life; complete the participant fields of the Article 988 fee exemption and deliver it to the district attorney BEFORE filing, expecting it back within fifteen days; request whichever Article 989 certification letters the chosen eligibility basis needs; file with the clerk with the fee or the returned exemption; the clerk serves the district attorney, the Bureau and the arresting agency under Article 979; agencies have sixty days from service to object under Article 980, extendable once by up to thirty days; an Affidavit of No Opposition from each named agency attached to the motion supports an ex parte grant with no contradictory hearing; if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment under Article 982. It also carries the Louisiana State Police list of common fatal errors: wrong arrest date, using the amended charge instead of the original arrest charge, omitting counts, putting misdemeanours and felonies in the wrong section, missing dispositions or certifications, and choosing the wrong eligibility basis. On this track the instructions add that Article 985(B) leaves the redacted record publicly available as to the other individuals named, that Article 985(C) relieves the clerk of liability where the order does not specify each location and the information to be redacted, and that whether redaction rather than full expungement is the correct request turns on who else appears in the record.

tracks.legalName: Expedited Expungement of Arrest Records for Certain Individuals (La. C.Cr.P. arts. 999, 999.1)
tracks.publicName: Free expedited clearing of an arrest from when you were seventeen

controllingAuthority.summary: Article 999(A) provides that a person shall be entitled to the expedited expungement of his arrest, at no cost to him, if the person meets all of the following: (1) the person is seventeen years of age when arrested or charged with any criminal offence under Title 14 or Title 40 of the Louisiana Revised Statutes of 1950; (2) the district attorney, for any reason, declined to prosecute all offences arising out of that arrest, including because the person successfully completed a pretrial diversion programme; and (3) prosecution was instituted and such proceedings have been finally disposed of by dismissal, sustaining of a motion to quash, or acquittal. Article 999(B) provides that the Article does not apply to any misdemeanour or felony conviction arising from the incident of arrest. Article 999(C) provides that the expedited expungement shall be served under Article 982. Article 972(1) defines expedited expungement as an order of expungement that a judge may sign pursuant to Article 999 WITHOUT THE INDIVIDUAL FILING A MOTION TO EXPUNGE WITH THE CLERK OF COURT. Article 999.1 supplies the order form to be used, which recites the three Article 999(A) conditions, provides the defendant-information fields and a six-entry service list, and carries the judge's signature line. Both Articles were added, and Articles 972 and 983(G) amended, by Acts 2024, No. 270, effective 1 August 2024.

exclusions: Any misdemeanour or felony conviction arising from the incident of arrest (Art. 999(B)).

A person who was not seventeen years of age when arrested or charged. The age element is objective and narrow: it is a legacy of Louisiana's raise-the-age transition and is not a general youthful-offender provision.
An arrest or charge for an offence outside Title 14 or Title 40 of the Louisiana Revised Statutes of 1950.

Applied as written, Article 999(A) requires all three conditions together, which means the route reaches only a person who was seventeen at arrest AND whose offences the district attorney declined to prosecute AND whose instituted prosecution was finally disposed of by dismissal, quashal or acquittal. This memo applies the statute as written because that is the narrower reading; the internal contradiction between (2) and (3) is preserved as an open question rather than resolved by construction.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Article 999(A) says the person must meet 'all of the following' and then lists (2) a declination to prosecute all offences arising out of the arrest and (3) an instituted prosecution finally disposed of by dismissal, quashal or acquittal. Read literally the two are mutually exclusive, because a declination means no prosecution was instituted, and almost nobody could qualify. The Acts 2024, No. 270 résumé digest repeats 'all of the following', and the Article 999.1 order form recites the same three conditions under the heading 'wherein all of the following applies', so both the statute and the prescribed order carry the cumulative formulation. Whether (2) and (3) are cumulative as written or alternative as they must sensibly be is unresolved, and it materially decides who the eligibility engine returns.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: The review left Track G unresolved and it is now resolved to process_guidance on the actual initiating act, not on the absence of a conventional motion. Article 972(1) affirmatively provides that the order is one a judge may sign without the individual filing a motion to expunge with the clerk of court; Article 986's mandatory-form list does not include Article 999.1; and no Article, form instruction or official Louisiana State Police material identifies any participant submission, application or written request. The route is nonetheless a real mechanism with objective eligibility conditions and no cost, so the guidance identifies the candidate, states the conditions, reproduces the order for reference and routes the participant to the district attorney and the court. Eligibility is applied as the statute is written — all three conditions — because that is the narrower reading and the safest supported treatment; the contradiction between (2) and (3) is preserved as an open question rather than cured by construction. Both open questions are release blockers on this track rather than build blockers, because what to implement today is known.

tracks.legalName: Automated Expungement of Qualifying Records (La. C.Cr.P. art. 985.2)

controllingAuthority.summary: Article 985.2(A) directs the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information to identify within its criminal repository database all records with a Case Management Information System number and final dispositions for individuals eligible for expungement under Articles 976, 977 and 978. Article 985.2(B) provides that beginning 1 January 2025 a defendant may submit a request through the Bureau for expungement through the automated process, the request containing the defendant's name, date of birth, last four digits of the Social Security number, arrest date and case number, and requires the Bureau to expunge any eligible records within thirty days of receipt and send them to the Louisiana Supreme Court Case Management Information System. Paragraphs (C) and (D) govern clerk verification and notice to the district attorney, sheriff and arresting agency. Article 985.2(G) provides that the Article shall be subject to the appropriate funding necessary for implementation and provided for in the executive budget for Fiscal Year 2025-2026. The current official text at legis.la.gov carries the operative note 'Article 985.2 eff. upon appropriation of monies by the Legislature. See Acts 2023, No. 454.' Section 4 of Acts 2023, No. 454 conditions the effectiveness of its substantive Sections on an Act or Acts originating in the 2023 Regular Session containing specific appropriations of monies for the office of state police, the Louisiana Supreme Court and the Louisiana Clerks' Remote Access Authority for the implementation of the Act. The route reaches only records already eligible under Articles 976, 977 and 978 and expands eligibility for no one.

exclusions: The Article is not established as effective. The current official text of the Code carries the note that Article 985.2 is effective upon appropriation of monies by the Legislature, citing Acts 2023, No. 454, and that note is still present on the Legislature's own current publication of the Article as of 3 August 2026.

The route does not expand eligibility. It reaches only records already eligible for expungement under Articles 976, 977 and 978, so a person not already eligible under those Articles gains nothing from it.
Records predating the automation window described in the Article are outside it.
The enacting legislation provided that no person shall have a cause of action resulting from the omission of their records from automated expungement.

controllingAuthority.summary: Article 985.3(A) provides that the court MAY ORDER the immediate expungement of the record of the arrest and conviction of the violation that necessitated participation in the probation or programme, by a person who is otherwise eligible for an expungement, upon the successful completion of a court-ordered probation or alternative sentencing programme. Article 985.3(B) provides that ONLY THE FORM PROVIDED IN ARTICLE 992 shall be used to expunge the record of such a person. Article 985.3(C) provides that the immediate expungement shall be served pursuant to Article 982 and shall include the court record with the signed order together with the bill of information, the sentencing minutes, and any documents or records relevant to the arrest incident and plea agreements, if available. The Article was enacted by Acts 2024, No. 560 (2024 H.B. 416), whose digest describes it as providing for a court-ordered automatic expungement in certain cases. The full text was obtained and read for this normalization; the review had identified the Article but not read it.

exclusions: A person who is not otherwise eligible for an expungement. Article 985.3(A) reaches only a person 'who is otherwise eligible for an expungement', so the underlying eligibility rules of Articles 976, 977 and 978, including every Article 977(C) and Article 978(B) exclusion, continue to govern. The Article shortens the path, not the eligibility test.
A record other than the record of the arrest and conviction of the violation that necessitated participation in the probation or programme. Other cases are outside it.
A person who did not successfully complete the court-ordered probation or alternative sentencing programme.
The relief is discretionary. Article 985.3(A) says the court 'may order', so no participant is entitled to it.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. The triggering event is the successful completion of the court-ordered probation or alternative sentencing programme, and the expungement is immediate on the court's order. Whether it displaces the Article 977(A)(2) five-year and Article 978(A)(2) ten-year waiting periods for an otherwise-eligible person is the open question below; the Article does not say so expressly, unlike Article 985.1(D), which disapplies them in terms.

components.notes: Guidance that states the mechanism from the text: on successful completion of a court-ordered probation or alternative sentencing programme, the court may order the immediate expungement of the record of the arrest and conviction of the violation that necessitated the probation or programme, for a person who is otherwise eligible for an expungement. It tells the participant that the Article prescribes no motion or application for them to file, that the relief is discretionary rather than an entitlement, that the underlying Article 976, 977 or 978 eligibility rules still govern, that Article 985.3(C) requires the served record to include the bill of information, the sentencing minutes and any documents relevant to the arrest incident and plea agreements, and that they should raise Article 985.3 with the court and with their own counsel at or before the completion proceeding. It also states that the ordinary Article 977 or 978 motion track remains available and does produce a packet.

The Article 992 order form is reproduced for reference only, because Article 985.3(B) provides that only that form shall be used. It is the judge's order of expungement and no field on it is completed here. If the initiation question is later answered in favour of a participant-prepared proposed order accompanying an ordinary Article 989 motion, that route is already modelled on the Article 977 and Article 978 tracks and is not duplicated here.

Article 985.3(A) says the court 'may order' the immediate expungement and prescribes no motion, application or request; Article 985.3(B) names only the Article 992 order form; Article 986's mandatory-form list assigns no motion form to the Article; and the Acts 2024, No. 560 digest describes it as a court-ordered automatic expungement. legalDesignDecision.rationale: The review identified Article 985.3 but had not read it; the complete current official text has now been obtained and analysed, and the strategy follows the actual mechanism rather than the article title. The eligible circumstance is a person who is otherwise eligible for an expungement and has successfully completed a court-ordered probation or alternative sentencing programme; the triggering event is that successful completion; the relief is discretionary because the court 'may order' it; the record reached is only that of the arrest and conviction of the violation that necessitated the probation or programme; venue is the sentencing court; no notice period and no contradictory hearing are prescribed; service is by the clerk under Article 982 with the bill of information, sentencing minutes and arrest and plea documents included; and the only form named is the Article 992 order, which is the judge's. The defendant is not directed to file anything, and Article 986 assigns no motion form to the Article. There is therefore no independently deliverable participant packet on this track today, so it is process_guidance — a substantive conclusion drawn from the text, not an inference from the title and not a placeholder. Its relationship to Articles 976 through 978 is that it presupposes their eligibility rules and does not displace them. The two questions that would change the strategy are release blockers on this track.

tracks.publicName: Set aside a conviction and dismiss the prosecution after a deferred sentence

controllingAuthority.summary: Article 987 supplies the forms to be used for a motion to set aside a conviction and dismiss the prosecution, the rule to show cause, and the order of dismissal. It is not an expungement. It is the predicate filing that converts a completed deferred sentence into a set-aside conviction and a dismissed prosecution under Article 894(B) for a misdemeanour or Article 893(E) for a felony, which in turn unlocks Article 977(A)(1) or Article 978(A)(1). As pleaded on the statutory form, eligibility is that the period of the deferred sentence has run and the petitioner has successfully completed the terms of probation. The instrument is in three parts: the Motion; a Rule to Show Cause ordering the district attorney to show cause why the motion should not be granted; and the Order of Dismissal. The motion's own prayer asks for relief after a contradictory hearing with the district attorney's office. Service is on the district attorney and on the attorney for the defendant or the defendant. The form carries parallel signature blocks for counsel and for an unrepresented mover, so it is drafted for pro se use. Source note Acts 2014, No. 145.

exclusions: A conviction that was not the subject of a deferred sentence under Article 893 or Article 894. Where no deferred sentence was imposed there is nothing to set aside, and the participant goes directly to the Article 977 or Article 978 waiting-period route instead.
A case where the period of the deferred sentence has not yet run.
A case where the terms of probation were not successfully completed.

components.notes: The Article 987 instrument, mandatory under Article 986, in three parts on one form: the Motion to Set Aside Conviction and Dismiss Prosecution, the Rule to Show Cause ordering the district attorney to show cause why the motion should not be granted, and the Order of Dismissal. The participant elects Article 894(B) for a misdemeanour or Article 893(E) for a felony. LegalEase completes the neutral participant and case fields — the caption, docket number, division, parties, the offence and statute, the sentencing date and the deferred-sentence and probation dates — and leaves the rule's return date, every judicial field and the order of dismissal blank. The factual assertion that the period of the deferred sentence has run and that the terms of probation were successfully completed is the participant's own and is never auto-completed.

Instructions covering: that this is not an expungement and does not itself clear any record; that it is the predicate that unlocks Article 977(A)(1) for a misdemeanour or Article 978(A)(1) for a felony, and that after the order of dismissal is signed the participant returns to that expungement track; that the rule to show cause is directed to the district attorney and the clerk obtains the return date; that the motion's prayer contemplates a contradictory hearing with the district attorney's office; that service is on the district attorney and on the defendant or the defendant's attorney; and that a dispute about whether probation was successfully completed, or any contradictory hearing, is where self-help ends.

provenance.sourceStatement: What it is: not an expungement. It is the predicate filing that converts a completed deferred sentence into a set-aside conviction and dismissed prosecution, which then unlocks Track B or Track D.

limitations.statement: The rule to show cause return date is set by the court and supplied by the clerk; leave it blank.

provenance.sourceHeading: TRACK J: Motion to set aside conviction and dismiss prosecution
provenance.sourceStatement: Procedure: the Art. 987 form is a three-part instrument: the Motion, a Rule to Show Cause ordering the district attorney to show cause why the motion should not be granted, and an Order of Dismissal.
